title: Botanicula: tiny eyes, unusual bodies and group staging

people.name: Jaromír Plachý
people.role: Animator and creator of Botanicula, as described on Amanita's official forum index

summary: The botanical cast shows how much character can survive when faces are a few tiny marks on strongly different bodies.

observations.text: In screenshot 04, several small protagonists cluster together on a branch opposite a huge hanging dark creature. Tiny bright eyes, very different body proportions and the distance between groups carry the scene; a detailed human face is unnecessary.

Screenshot 03 repeats a one-eyed creature at different sizes. The large foreground eye gives a clear directional cue, while the surrounding small versions retain the same instantly readable eye-and-body arrangement.
In the archived IndieCade interview, Plachý and Stehlík describe nature and an old garden as inspiration; they also say the musicians saw animations during the collaboration.

mistIdeas: Our inference: let a shift of attention move the whole eye pair or head toward a specific target, then hold. Avoid continual wandering that has no apparent object.
Our inference: try quiet listening with a nearly still face and a slight body lean. Contrast will give the next clear reaction more weight.
Our inference: borrow the clarity of silhouette and gaze, not the botanical textures or character shapes.

title: Farewell North - making the human companion responsive

people.name: Kyle Banks
people.role: Developer and author of the facial-animation devlog

summary: A solo developer documents the difficult jump from a face that merely exists to a character who can carry close dialogue.

observations.text: Banks reports that his human protagonist initially had to be kept distant or off-screen. His devlog describes adding eye tracking, blinking, expressions and lip sync with Unity, Blender and FaceIt.
He warns in his own description that expressions can quickly feel wrong and still require refinement; hiring animators and adding believable behaviour alone had not resolved the lifeless face.

mistIdeas: Our inference: review MIST at its actual conversation size, because a small distant character can conceal a weak face.
Our inference: evaluate gaze, blink, expression and speech as separate contributions; freeze three channels while judging the fourth, then restore them together.

title: Klei: hand-drawn appeal with reusable animation symbols
summary: A production reference for keeping an expressive design consistent across reusable game animation states.

observations.text: The official session overview covers character design, polished symbol animation, costume and colour swapping, animation reuse, and working with designers to refine responsiveness.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep reusable neutral eye and mouth symbols, but allow purpose-drawn replacements for extreme expressions.
Our inference: map expressions to actual dialogue or game events, with explicit entry and recovery states. This is an implementation proposal, not an observed Klei facial sequence.
